title: ARDS and refractory hypoxaemia
summary: Diagnose ARDS with the 2024 global definition (including SpO2/FiO2 and ultrasound for resource-limited settings), ventilate with 6 mL/kg PBW and plateau ≤ 30, choose PEEP sensibly, prone early for P/F < 150, use neuromuscular blockade and conservative fluids selectively, consider steroids, and refer for ECMO in time.

topics.title: Defining and diagnosing ARDS
topics.summary: ARDS is acute (≤ 1 week) hypoxaemic respiratory failure with bilateral opacities not fully explained by cardiac failure or fluid overload. The 2024 global definition adds non-intubated patients on HFNC ≥ 30 L/min, SpO2/FiO2 criteria, and lung ultrasound for resource-limited settings.

definition.text: Global definition 2024: risk factor, onset within 1 week, bilateral opacities (CXR, CT or ultrasound), not fully explained by cardiac failure or fluid overload, and hypoxaemia: non-intubated P/F ≤ 300 or S/F ≤ 315 (SpO2 ≤ 97%) on HFNO ≥ 30 L/min or NIV/CPAP ≥ 5 cmH2O; intubated graded by P/F (or S/F) with PEEP ≥ 5.

steps.title: Risk factor
steps.detail: Pneumonia (bacterial, viral, tropical such as leptospirosis, scrub typhus, malaria, dengue), sepsis, aspiration, pancreatitis, trauma, transfusion (TRALI), drowning, burns.

steps.title: Timing and imaging
steps.detail: Onset within 1 week of insult or new/worsening symptoms; bilateral opacities on CXR/CT, or bilateral B-lines/consolidations on ultrasound by a trained operator.

steps.title: Cardiogenic oedema
steps.detail: Echo (LV function, valves, filling pressures), BNP, fluid balance. ARDS can coexist with heart failure.

steps.title: Treat it
steps.detail: Cultures, respiratory PCR, tropical serology (module 25), procalcitonin; CT if unclear; bronchoscopy/BAL in immunocompromised.

redFlags.text: P/F < 150 on PEEP ≥ 5: prone positioning indicated (next topics).
P/F < 80 for > 6 h despite optimisation: refer for ECMO now.

pitfalls.text: Calling every bilateral infiltrate ARDS without an echo.
Using S/F when SpO2 is 98-100% (flat part of the curve; invalid).

pearls.text: Leptospirosis pulmonary haemorrhage and falciparum malaria are important ARDS causes in Indian monsoon months.

nodes.text: Within 1 week of a risk factor or new symptoms?
Consider chronic or other diagnoses (ILD, malignancy)
Fully explained by cardiac failure or fluid (echo)?
ARDS: grade severity, lung-protective strategy, treat cause

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Diffuse alveolar damage: endothelial and epithelial injury, protein-rich oedema, surfactant loss, atelectasis and shunt, followed by a fibroproliferative phase. Lung compliance falls because the aerated lung is small ("baby lung").
consultantNotes.evidence:
- **Berlin 2012:** timing, imaging, origin of oedema and P/F categories with PEEP ≥ 5.
- **Global definition 2024:** extends Berlin to HFNO patients, allows S/F and ultrasound, and adds resource-limited criteria.
- **ESICM 2023:** endorses an extended definition and recommends against using phenotypes to guide care outside trials.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Including HFNO patients increases ARDS incidence; trials using Berlin criteria may not apply directly.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes:
- Many Indian ICUs, especially district hospitals, lack frequent ABG or CT; the S/F + ultrasound criteria make ARDS recognisable there.
- Tropical infections (leptospirosis, scrub typhus, malaria, dengue, H1N1 influenza) are leading ARDS causes in India; seasonal peaks follow the monsoon.

topics.title: Lung-protective ventilation and PEEP
topics.summary: Tidal volume 6 mL/kg PBW (4-8), plateau ≤ 30 cmH2O, driving pressure ideally ≤ 15, PEEP by table or mechanics (higher PEEP in moderate-severe ARDS), no prolonged recruitment manoeuvres, permissive hypercapnia with pH ≥ 7.20-7.25.

steps.title: Vt 6 mL/kg PBW
steps.detail: Begin at 8 and reduce to 6 within 1-4 h; 4-5 if Pplat > 30.

steps.title: Plateau and driving pressure
steps.detail: Pplat ≤ 30 cmH2O (0.5 s inspiratory hold). Driving pressure ≤ 15 cmH2O where possible.

steps.title: Choose a strategy
steps.detail: Mild: lower PEEP/FiO2 table. Moderate-severe: higher PEEP (without prolonged recruitment) suggested by ATS 2024; watch Pplat, BP and compliance response.

steps.title: Prolonged recruitment manoeuvres
steps.detail: Strong recommendation against prolonged/stepwise recruitment (ART trial harm).

steps.title: Permissive hypercapnia
steps.detail: Rate up to 35/min to keep pH ≥ 7.20-7.25 (watch auto-PEEP). Avoid hypercapnia in raised ICP and severe RV failure.

steps.title: Targets
steps.detail: SpO2 88-95% (PaO2 55-80 mmHg) per ARDSNet protocol.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.detail: P/F < 150: prone (next topic); consider NMB; optimise fluids; then ECMO referral.

redFlags.text: Pplat > 30 despite Vt 4 mL/kg: severe disease; prone, consider ECMO.
Hypotension after PEEP increase: preload, RV failure, overdistension; reduce PEEP and echo.

pitfalls.text: Using actual body weight for Vt.
Forgetting to measure plateau after every Vt or PEEP change.

pearls.text: If compliance improves and driving pressure falls after a PEEP increase, the lung recruited; if Pplat rises with no compliance change, it overdistended.

nodes.text: Vt 6 mL/kg PBW; PEEP per table; SpO2 88-95%
Continue; daily reassessment and SAT/SBT when ready

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ARMA (2000):** 6 vs 12 mL/kg reduced mortality.
- **ALVEOLI (2004):** higher vs lower PEEP: no difference overall; later meta-analyses suggest benefit in moderate-severe ARDS.
- **ART (2017):** recruitment + titrated PEEP increased mortality.
- **ATS 2024:** higher PEEP without prolonged LRM in moderate-severe ARDS (conditional); against prolonged LRM (strong).
- **ESICM 2023:** recommends low Vt (≤ 6 mL/kg PBW) and recommends against prolonged high-pressure recruitment manoeuvres.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Individualised PEEP (oesophageal pressure, EIT, recruitment-to-inflation ratio) has not consistently improved outcomes.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Plateau measurement is possible on almost all ICU ventilators; make it a nursing chart item every 4 h.

topics.title: Prone positioning
topics.summary: Prone early (within 36 h) when P/F < 150 mmHg on FiO2 ≥ 0.6 and PEEP ≥ 5 despite optimisation, for at least 16 h per session, using a trained team and a checklist. Repeat daily until P/F ≥ 150 is sustained supine.

steps.title: P/F < 150
steps.detail: On FiO2 ≥ 0.6, PEEP ≥ 5, Vt ~6 mL/kg after 12-24 h stabilisation.

steps.title: Check
steps.detail: Unstable spine, open abdomen, raised ICP, massive haemoptysis, recent sternotomy, unstable fractures, pregnancy (relative), haemodynamic instability (relative).

steps.title: Team of 5
steps.detail: Team leader at head (airway); pre-oxygenate FiO2 1.0; secure tube and lines; empty stomach; protect eyes; ECG leads to the back; pads for face, chest, pelvis, knees.

steps.title: Sheet technique
steps.detail: Envelope with sheets, lateral, then prone; arms in swimmer's position (alternate every 2-4 h); head turned and repositioned every 2-4 h.

steps.title: ≥ 16 h
steps.detail: Sessions ≥ 16 h (PROSEVA mean ~17 h).

steps.title: Criteria
steps.detail: P/F ≥ 150 with PEEP ≤ 10 and FiO2 ≤ 0.6 at least 4 h after turning supine; or complications.

redFlags.text: Accidental extubation or line loss during turn: airway team at head, plan in advance.
Facial pressure sores and ocular injury: check every 2 h.

pitfalls.text: Proning late (after days) or for short sessions (< 12 h).
Stopping proning because oxygenation did not improve immediately (benefit is not only through oxygenation).

pearls.text: Enteral feeding can continue in prone position (reverse Trendelenburg 10-25°).
CPR in prone position is possible (compress between scapulae) while preparing to turn.

nodes.text: Prone ≥ 16 h with trained team and checklist

consultantNotes.pathophysiology: Prone positioning makes lung inflation more homogeneous (the heart and abdomen compress less lung), recruits dorsal regions, improves V/Q matching and reduces ventilator-induced lung injury. It also unloads the RV.
consultantNotes.evidence:
- **PROSEVA (2013):** early prolonged proning (mean ~17 h/day) in P/F < 150 reduced 28-day mortality (16.0% vs 32.8%).
- **ESICM 2023 and ATS (2017, reaffirmed):** prone ≥ 12-16 h/day in moderate-severe ARDS.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Awake proning in non-intubated patients helped COVID-19 (meta-trial) but is unproven in other causes.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Proning needs no equipment beyond pillows and staff; it is the most cost-effective ARDS intervention for Indian ICUs. Train nurses with simulation.

topics.title: Neuromuscular blockade and fluid management
topics.summary: Use a 24-48 h cisatracurium infusion in early severe ARDS if asynchrony or high pressures persist despite deep sedation. After shock resolves, use a conservative fluid strategy with diuretics to reduce lung water.

steps.title: Early severe ARDS
steps.detail: P/F < 150 with persistent ventilator dyssynchrony, double triggering, or Pplat/driving pressure above target despite deep sedation. Not routine.

steps.title: Sedate deeply first
steps.detail: RASS -5 before paralysis (awareness risk); then cisatracurium bolus and infusion for up to 48 h.

steps.title: During NMB
steps.detail: Train-of-four, eye care, pressure areas, DVT prophylaxis, glucose; daily reassess the need. Avoid steroids + NMB for long periods (weakness).

steps.title: Shock phase
steps.detail: Resuscitate shock appropriately; no restriction during shock.

steps.title: After shock
steps.detail: Conservative strategy: aim even to negative balance; furosemide if CVP or clinical overload and perfusion adequate (FACTT).

steps.title: Selected
steps.detail: Albumin + furosemide in hypoalbuminaemic patients may improve oxygenation (small trials).

doseCards.dose: 0.15-0.2 mg/kg bolus, then 1-3 mcg/kg/min (ACURASYS: 15 mg then 37.5 mg/h)
doseCards.workedExample: 70 kg × 2 mcg/kg/min = 140 mcg/min = 8.4 mg/h ÷ 2 mg/mL = 4.2 mL/h

redFlags.text: Paralysed patient with tachycardia and hypertension: inadequate sedation (awareness).

pitfalls.text: Using NMB to mask a ventilator setting problem that could be fixed.
Prolonged infusions beyond 48 h without daily review.

pearls.text: In ROSE (lighter sedation controls), early NMB did not reduce mortality; reserve for those who need it.

nodes.text: Persistent asynchrony or high Pplat/ΔP despite deep sedation and setting changes?
Cisatracurium ≤ 48 h with deep sedation; TOF monitoring
Conservative fluids: diuretics to even or negative balance

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ACURASYS (2010):** 48 h cisatracurium in early P/F < 150 improved adjusted 90-day survival.
- **ROSE (2019):** early NMB with deep sedation vs usual care with lighter sedation: no mortality difference.
- **ATS 2024:** suggests NMB in early severe ARDS (conditional).
- **FACTT (2006):** conservative fluid strategy increased ventilator-free days without more organ failure.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Cisatracurium supply is intermittent in some Indian hospitals; atracurium or vecuronium (with renal/hepatic caution) are pragmatic substitutes.

quiz.stem: NMB in ARDS is best reserved for:
options: Early severe ARDS with persistent asynchrony or high pressures
quiz.explanation: ROSE showed no benefit for routine early NMB.
More ventilator-free days, no mortality difference.

topics.title: Corticosteroids and pharmacological adjuncts
topics.summary: ATS 2024 suggests corticosteroids for ARDS. Use an evidence-based regimen matched to the cause (dexamethasone for COVID-19 and DEXA-ARDS; hydrocortisone for severe CAP). Avoid in influenza. Inhaled vasodilators improve oxygenation but not survival.

steps.title: Steroid candidate
steps.detail: Moderate-severe ARDS, early (< 14 days), no contraindication (uncontrolled infection, influenza, fungal infection).

steps.title: Non-COVID ARDS
steps.detail: Dexamethasone 20 mg IV daily days 1-5, then 10 mg days 6-10 (DEXA-ARDS).

steps.title: Severe CAP
steps.detail: Hydrocortisone 200 mg/day for 4-8 days then taper (CAPE COD).

steps.title: COVID-19
steps.detail: Dexamethasone 6 mg daily up to 10 days.

steps.title: Side effects
steps.detail: Glucose, new infection, weakness; stop if alternative diagnosis or harm.

steps.title: Inhaled pulmonary vasodilators
steps.detail: Inhaled nitric oxide or epoprostenol as short-term rescue for refractory hypoxaemia or RV failure; no mortality benefit.

doseCards.dose: 20 mg daily days 1-5, then 10 mg daily days 6-10
200 mg/day × 4 days (8 if not improving), then taper
doseCards.dilution: 200 mg in 50 mL NS at ~2.1 mL/h

redFlags.text: Influenza ARDS: steroids associated with higher mortality in observational data; avoid unless another indication.

pitfalls.text: Starting steroids late (> 14 days) in fibroproliferative ARDS (older ARDSNet LaSRS trial showed harm).

pearls.text: Check strongyloides risk (eosinophilia, endemic areas including India) before prolonged steroids; consider empirical ivermectin.

nodes.text: Influenza, untreated fungal infection, or > 14 days?

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **ATS 2024:** suggests corticosteroids for ARDS (conditional, moderate certainty).
- **DEXA-ARDS (2020):** dexamethasone increased ventilator-free days and reduced 60-day mortality in moderate-severe ARDS.
- **CAPE COD (2023):** hydrocortisone reduced 28-day mortality in severe CAP (6.2% vs 11.9%).
- **RECOVERY (2021):** dexamethasone reduced mortality in ventilated COVID-19.
consultantNotes.controversies: - Optimal drug, dose and duration; heterogeneity of ARDS causes.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - Screen for strongyloidiasis and latent TB in high-prevalence settings before prolonged steroids; consider empirical ivermectin 200 mcg/kg for 1-2 days.

quiz.stem: Steroids should generally be avoided in ARDS due to:

options: Improves oxygenation transiently without survival benefit

verify.reason: Practice recommendation from infectious disease literature; not in the ARDS guidelines cited.

topics.title: Refractory hypoxaemia and VV-ECMO
topics.summary: If P/F stays < 80 mmHg (or < 50 for 3 h) or pH < 7.25 with PaCO2 ≥ 60 despite optimised ventilation, proning and NMB, refer early to an ECMO centre (EOLIA criteria). Transfer before the patient is too unstable.

steps.title: Check the basics
steps.detail: Vt 6 mL/kg, PEEP appropriate, proned, NMB, conservative fluids, treat infection, drain effusions, exclude pneumothorax and RV failure (echo).

steps.title: EOLIA
steps.detail: P/F < 50 for > 3 h, or P/F < 80 for > 6 h, or pH < 7.25 with PaCO2 ≥ 60 mmHg for > 6 h (RR 35, Pplat ≤ 32).

steps.title: Early
steps.detail: Contact the ECMO centre early (within 7 days of ventilation preferred); discuss transfer or mobile ECMO retrieval.

steps.title: Consider
steps.detail: Ventilation > 7-10 days with high pressures, irreversible disease without transplant option, severe brain injury, contraindication to anticoagulation, very poor baseline. See module 14.

steps.title: Rescue
steps.detail: Inhaled vasodilator, higher PEEP trial, sustained prone, accept SpO2 85-88%.

redFlags.text: Severe RV failure (acute cor pulmonale) on echo: reduce PEEP/PaCO2, prone, consider VV or VA ECMO.

pitfalls.text: Referring after 10 days of injurious ventilation.

pearls.text: Calculate the Murray (LIS) score and RESP score when discussing referral.

nodes.text: Severe ARDS, P/F < 100 despite lung-protective ventilation
Check DOPES, effusions, pneumothorax, RV function; optimise PEEP
Maximal conventional therapy; discuss goals of care

consultantNotes.evidence:
- **CESAR (2009):** referral to an ECMO centre improved 6-month survival without disability.
- **EOLIA (2018):** 60-day mortality 35% vs 46% (not statistically significant; 28% crossover); post-hoc Bayesian analysis favoured ECMO.
- **ATS 2024:** VV-ECMO in selected severe ARDS (conditional).
consultantNotes.controversies: - Which patients benefit; transfer risks; resource allocation.
consultantNotes.indiaNotes: - VV-ECMO is available in a limited number of Indian tertiary and private centres; costs are a major barrier. Identify your nearest ECMO centre and its referral criteria in advance.

quiz.explanation: Also P/F < 80 for > 6 h or pH < 7.25 with PaCO2 ≥ 60.
Referral strategy improved survival without disability.

quiz.stem: Before ECMO referral, which is essential?
quiz.explanation: Prone positioning is a cheap, proven therapy.

drugs.name: Cisatracurium
drugs.indications: Early severe ARDS (P/F < 150) with persistent asynchrony or high plateau pressure despite deep sedation; prone positioning.
drugs.adultDose: Bolus 0.15-0.2 mg/kg, then 1-3 mcg/kg/min (ACURASYS used a fixed 15 mg bolus then 37.5 mg/h for 48 h).
drugs.preparationIndia: 2 mg/mL (5 mL and 10 mL vials); 100 mg in 50 mL = 2 mg/mL undiluted.
drugs.renalHepatic: Hofmann elimination: no adjustment in renal or hepatic failure.
drugs.cautions: Must be deeply sedated first (awareness). ICU-acquired weakness with prolonged use; eye care and pressure care.
drugs.monitoring: Train-of-four (aim 1-2 twitches if titrating), sedation depth (BIS if available).

drugs.name: Atracurium
drugs.cautions: Histamine release (hypotension, bronchospasm) with fast boluses; laudanosine accumulation (seizure risk theoretical).

drugs.name: Dexamethasone
drugs.indications: Moderate-severe ARDS (DEXA-ARDS regimen); COVID-19 requiring oxygen (6 mg daily for 10 days).
drugs.adultDose: DEXA-ARDS: 20 mg IV daily days 1-5, then 10 mg daily days 6-10. COVID-19: 6 mg daily up to 10 days.
drugs.preparationIndia: 4 mg/mL (2 mL and 30 mL vials) and 8 mg/2 mL ampoules.
drugs.cautions: Hyperglycaemia; secondary infections; avoid in influenza ARDS (observational harm).

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone
drugs.adultDose: 200 mg/day infusion for 4 days (or 8 days if not improving), then taper over 8-14 days total.
drugs.cautions: CAPE COD excluded influenza and septic shock patients; hyperglycaemia.

drugs.name: Furosemide
drugs.indications: Conservative fluid strategy once shock has resolved (FACTT).
drugs.adultDose: 20-40 mg IV boluses, or infusion 5-20 mg/h, titrated to negative fluid balance with CVP/perfusion monitoring.
drugs.cautions: Hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, metabolic alkalosis, ototoxicity at high bolus doses.

verify.reason: Cisatracurium 2 mg/mL is available in India but may be short-supplied; atracurium and vecuronium are common substitutes. Doses given for both.
Steroid regimens in ARDS vary (dexamethasone DEXA-ARDS, methylprednisolone Meduri, hydrocortisone for severe CAP). ATS 2024 suggests corticosteroids without specifying a single regimen.
